_meta.description: Synthetic dossier fixture for local development and manual testing. Contains five findings that exercise all QA/Critic paths: identity check (PASS), identity mismatch (PASS — structurally valid), reference-standard section (PASS), missing citation (FLAG), and deliberately out-of-range score (FLAG → ESCALATE via section rule).
changes_from_v1.0: F-003 rationale and evidence updated to include all IPRP S.5 sub-item keywords (lot number, CoA, working standard, source) so it correctly PASSes the QA/Critic. The S.5 agent (s5_standards.py) still returns NON_COMPLIANT for the outdated BP 2019 edition — that is unaffected.
F-005 uncertainty_score corrected from 100 (boundary-valid, would PASS) to 150 (out of range, triggers R2 FLAG). The _meta already described this intent; the data now matches it.
F-004 and F-005 are both in 3.2.S.3 — with F-005 now correctly FLAGging, two findings in 3.2.S.3 are flagged, triggering the section escalation rule. Both are promoted to ESCALATE.

findings_notes.F-001: PASS — CAS number and INN are consistent. Baseline clean finding. R1-R3 all pass.
findings_notes.F-002: PASS — CAS mismatch noted in rationale; finding is structurally valid (citation present, score in range, tone consistent). The regulatory concern (wrong CAS) is captured in the rationale for the assessor — QA/Critic does not make identity verdicts.
findings_notes.F-003: PASS — Outdated-standard claim (BP 2019 vs current BP 2024); well-formed finding. All IPRP S.5 sub-item keywords present (lot, CoA, working standard, source) so R4-R7 do not fire. The S.5 agent (s5_standards.py / check_s5_claim) returns NON_COMPLIANT for the edition mismatch — that is separate from QA/Critic.
findings_notes.F-004: ESCALATE (promoted) — Empty citation field triggers R1 (FLAG). Promoted to ESCALATE because F-005 also FLAGs in the same section 3.2.S.3, reaching the ≥2 threshold.
findings_notes.F-005: ESCALATE (promoted) — uncertainty_score=150 is intentionally out of range [0,100]; triggers R2 (FLAG). Promoted to ESCALATE together with F-004 by the section rule. Test: test_mock_findings_f005_out_of_range_score_is_flagged.

_meta.do_not_use_for: All-PASS assertions. Use tests/golden/scenario_pass.json for that.

findings.rationale: The declared CAS number 64-17-5 matches the INN 'Ethanol' and is consistent with the evidence provided.
findings.evidence_snippet: Sponsor declares drug substance as Ethanol, CAS 64-17-5, BP grade.

findings.rationale: The declared CAS number 50-00-0 does not match the declared INN 'Ethanol'. CAS 50-00-0 refers to Formaldehyde, not Ethanol. This discrepancy is flagged for assessor review.
findings.evidence_snippet: Sponsor declares drug substance as Ethanol, CAS 50-00-0.

findings.rationale: Sponsor claims compliance with BP 2019 edition. The current edition at submission date (2024-03-01) was BP 2024. Editions differ — a non-compliance verdict will be issued by the S.5 agent. Lot number BP-ETH-2019-042 cited. Certificate of analysis (CoA) submitted. Working standard WS-ETH-LAB-001 qualified against BP primary reference standard. Source of reference standards: British Pharmacopoeia Commission.
findings.evidence_snippet: CoA submitted. Lot no. BP-ETH-2019-042. Working standard traceability confirmed. Source: BP Commission. Edition BP 2019 claimed; current edition at submission date is BP 2024.

findings.rationale: Residual solvent levels reported are within ICH Q3C Class 2 limits.
findings.evidence_snippet: GC analysis shows acetonitrile at 380 ppm; ICH Q3C limit is 410 ppm.
D90 value of 45 µm reported; specification states ≤ 50 µm.
